thesis: MU's ~18% 60-day decline appears driven mainly by headline/litigation risk (a new Netlist ITC patent-infringement complaint filed Aug 12, 2026 covering DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM products, plus an early-stage DRAM price-fixing class action against Micron, Samsung and SK hynix) and geopolitical uncertainty (reports the administration may let Apple source memory from Chinese suppliers CXMT/YMTC), layered on top of profit-taking after MU's large one-year run; underlying memory fundamentals (DRAM/NAND contract pricing reportedly up sharply this quarter, persistent supply tightness) still look intact per sell-side commentary. This suggests the pullback reflects sentiment and unresolved legal/policy overhangs more than a confirmed deterioration in Micron's business, but the read is far from clean given multiple unresolved threads and an earnings report due Sep 30, 2026 that could move the stock either way.
invalidation: Invalidate this thesis if Micron's Sep 30, 2026 earnings/guidance show DRAM/NAND pricing or demand rolling over, if the administration formally clears Apple to source meaningful volumes from CXMT/YMTC in a way that pressures Micron's US pricing power, or if the Netlist ITC case or the DRAM price-fixing class action advances to an adverse ruling, exclusion order, or material settlement against Micron.

thesis: The 60-day decline is best explained by a mix of sector-wide AI-capex skepticism (a broad semiconductor selloff in July 2026), competitive uncertainty over hyperscaler custom-silicon share (analyst reports, not company-confirmed, of Marvell losing Amazon Trainium3/4 design work to Alchip and Microsoft weighing a shift of Maia business to Broadcom), and dilution concerns from the ~59M-share warrant Marvell granted Google on August 19, 2026 in an expanded custom-chip deal — that warrant news alone triggered a further ~6% single-day drop despite being framed as a positive deal win. Notably, the August 27, 2026 Q2 FY27 earnings report beat estimates (record $2.74B revenue, up 37% YoY) and raised both FY27 and FY28 guidance, yet the stock still fell roughly 2-3% on the print, indicating the move is driven by positioning/sentiment and unresolved competitive/dilution overhang rather than a single confirmed fundamental deterioration.
invalidation: This avoid stance would be invalidated if Marvell confirms retention (not just rumored loss) of its Amazon and Microsoft custom-silicon programs and the stock stabilizes/reverses higher post-earnings; conversely, a confirmed loss of a major hyperscaler contract or a guidance cut would confirm further downside risk rather than invalidate it.
sources: 24/7 Wall St (Google warrant dilution overtakes deal rally): https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/21/marvell-sinks-6-as-google-warrant-dilution-overtakes-the-deal-rally-broadcom-ticks-up/

thesis: AAPL's 60-day advance is explained by a confirmed, company-disclosed Q3 FY2026 earnings beat (reported July 30, 2026, EPS $1.91 vs. $1.89 est., revenue $109.42B vs. $108.65B est.) driven by 22% year-over-year iPhone unit growth, even though that same report included softer forward guidance citing supply constraints that triggered an immediate ~6% post-earnings pullback. The rally reflects a real fundamental beat rather than a sector-wide or technical move, but with the September 9 iPhone launch event (the first under incoming CEO John Ternus, who takes over September 1 as Tim Cook becomes Executive Chairman) still ahead as an unresolved near-term catalyst, durability of the move is not yet confirmed.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if the September 9 iPhone launch underwhelms on demand/sell-through signals, or if Apple confirms the supply constraints flagged in Q3 guidance are worsening or extending into the holiday quarter, undercutting the fundamental read behind the rally.
sources: SCOTUSblog (Apple v. Epic Games cert grant, no argument date set): https://www.scotusblog.com/cases/apple-inc-v-epic-games-inc-2/

thesis: The 60-day decline traces to a mix of company-specific and mechanical pressures rather than one clean catalyst: an Aug 4, 2026 Q2 earnings beat on revenue (92% YoY growth) was overshadowed by a sixfold jump in capex to $18.4B (mostly AI/xAI infrastructure) alongside a continued $541M net loss, compounded by two Starship execution setbacks (a May Flight 12 Super Heavy booster mishap under FAA review and a July 16 Flight 13 launch abort) and an Aug 6 unlock of ~911.5M insider shares that expanded tradable float. A pending NAACP-led Clean Air Act injunction targeting SpaceXAI's Southaven power plant, which could curtail the Grok/xAI compute buildout, remains unresolved with its Aug 24 hearing postponed and no confirmed new date, leaving a real but unscheduled overhang alongside broader risk-off macro pressure on growth names.
invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated (i.e., reassessed) if the Southaven Clean Air Act injunction hearing gets a confirmed date and/or produces a shutdown or curtailment order for SpaceXAI's power operations, if Starship suffers another launch failure or FAA grounding, or if the next earnings report shows capex continuing to outpace revenue/EBITDA growth without a credible narrowing path to profitability.
sources: TechCrunch (FAA orders Starship V3 booster investigation): https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/27/faa-orders-spacex-to-investigate-starship-v3-booster-failure/

thesis: The 60-day decline is substantively explained by a confirmed, company-specific $20B dilutive common stock offering (upsized and priced at $95/share on Aug 10, 2026, now trading below that level) layered on top of persistent Intel Foundry operating losses ($2.8B in Q2 2026, projected to consume over $10B through 2027) and continued CPU market-share erosion to AMD, even though Intel's Q2 2026 revenue and EPS both beat guidance by wide margins. Because the sell-off reflects a mix of genuine dilution/execution concerns and a broader semiconductor sector pullback rather than a single isolated shock, and a Supreme Court hearing on an Intel 401(k) ERISA case is scheduled for October 2026, this reads as an unresolved, multi-factor situation rather than a clean mispricing.
invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated if Intel Foundry shows two consecutive quarters of narrowing operating losses with confirmed external 18A/14A customer commitments, and the stock stabilizes durably above the $95 offering price without further dilutive issuance.

thesis: AMD's ~11% 60-day decline coincides with a broad semiconductor/AI-sentiment selloff (rising 30-year Treasury yields, AI-overspending fears, and competitive chatter such as reports of DeepSeek developing its own AI processor) rather than company-specific fundamental deterioration: AMD's Q2 2026 results beat expectations with record $11.5B revenue (+50% YoY) and data center revenue +107% YoY, and management raised Q3 guidance to ~$13B, even though shares still sold off post-earnings as previously elevated AI expectations met a sell-the-news reaction across chip stocks. No AMD-specific confirmed negative catalyst, scheduled near-term litigation ruling, or governance red flag was identified in this research pass.
invalidation: This thesis is invalidated if a confirmed AMD-specific negative catalyst emerges (e.g., a data center/MI-series/Helios demand miss, a materially worse China export-control restriction cutting guidance, a guidance cut versus the current outlook, or a newly filed litigation/regulatory action naming AMD with a scheduled hearing or ruling) that shows the decline was driven by company fundamentals rather than sector-wide sentiment.
sources: The Globe and Mail (AMD Chief Accounting Officer resignation, Aug 2025): https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/AMD/pressreleases/34403825/amd-announces-resignation-of-chief-accounting-officer/

thesis: DELL's ~12% 60-day rise is driven by sustained momentum in AI server demand rather than a single new fundamentals catalyst inside the window: an already-confirmed August 4-6, 2026 disclosure that AI infrastructure startup Volta selected Dell as technology provider for a $10 billion, 133MW AI-factory partnership in Norway, plus analyst price-target increases (e.g., Evercore ISI to $500 on July 8, 2026) reaffirming Dell's AI server execution following its record Q1 FY2027 results. This is a company-specific, disclosed deal rather than a rumor or pure sector-wide move, but the read carries risk because Dell's next earnings report (Q2 FY2027) is scheduled for September 1, 2026 -- an unresolved binary event that historically moves the stock by an average of ~11.6% and could reverse the recent gains.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if the September 1, 2026 Q2 FY2027 earnings report shows an AI server order/backlog miss, a guidance cut, or management commentary indicating AI infrastructure demand (including the Volta partnership) is slowing, or if the stock retraces below the pre-rally level (~$415-430) on weakening fundamentals rather than short-term profit-taking.

thesis: The 2.36x volume spike is explained by NVIDIA's fiscal Q2 FY2027 earnings release (reported after close Aug 26, 2026), which beat consensus EPS/revenue and included guidance for continued strong revenue growth into the next fiscal year, easing prior AI-spending-slowdown fears; shares surged roughly 8.7% on Aug 27 on heavy institutional turnover. Even though the stock already rallied sharply post-print and now trades within about 4% of its 52-week high — meaning much of the good news may already be reflected in price — the catalyst is a confirmed, company-disclosed operating/guidance event rather than a rumor or technical signal, and no scheduled litigation, regulatory ruling, or governance red flag was found that would offset the read.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if subsequent disclosures (next quarterly report/guidance update, or an interim 8-K) show data-center/AI demand or revenue growth decelerating materially below the guidance given Aug 26, 2026, or if a newly scheduled adverse antitrust/export-control ruling or enforcement action materially restricts NVIDIA's AI-chip shipments.

thesis: OKTA's volume spike and fresh 52-week high are directly explained by a confirmed, company-disclosed Q2 FY27 earnings beat reported August 26, 2026 (revenue $805M vs. ~$795M consensus, adjusted EPS $1.05 vs. ~$0.97 consensus, RPO up 17% to $4.86B) paired with raised full-year FY27 revenue and EPS guidance, which drove a roughly 29% single-day rally and a wave of price-target increases from Morgan Stanley, RBC, BofA, Citizens and others. Even though the stock has already made an outsized one-day move and now trades within about 1% of its 52-week high — raising the risk of near-term profit-taking or mean reversion — the read is grounded in a specific, already-realized fundamental catalyst (beat-and-raise plus accelerating subscription backlog) rather than rumor, technical pattern, or sector-wide sentiment, and no pending litigation, restatement, or executive-departure issue was found that would undercut it.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if OKTA gives back this earnings-driven breakout by falling back toward/below its pre-earnings level (~$135, the Aug 26, 2026 close) on above-average volume, or if Q3 FY27 results/guidance (expected on or around December 2, 2026) fail to confirm the growth and RPO acceleration implied by this quarter's beat.

thesis: Salesforce reported a company-disclosed, blowout Q2 FY2027 earnings beat on August 26, 2026 (revenue $11.35B vs. $11.32B est.; adjusted EPS $5.90 vs. $3.27 est.), raised FY2027 revenue and EPS guidance, and announced an expanded Anthropic partnership ('Claudeforce') bringing Salesforce data and pre-built sales skills to Claude users — driving the stock up ~22.6% on the day at 4.4x average volume, which explains the bulk of the 60-day, +30% move. Even though management simultaneously cut FY2027 free-cash-flow growth guidance from 9-10% to 4-5% and gross debt roughly tripled (to ~$39.3B) to fund a $25B debt-financed accelerated share buyback, this reflects a deliberate capital-allocation trade-off layered on top of raised revenue/EPS guidance and 81% YoY free cash flow growth in the reported quarter, not a deterioration in the underlying business, and every major sell-side firm raised price targets after the print.
invalidation: Thesis invalidates if Salesforce's next quarterly report (expected ~early December 2026) shows decelerating AI/Agentforce bookings or a guidance cut, or if the leveraged balance sheet (gross debt ~$39.3B following the $25B ASR settling in October 2026) shows signs of credit-rating pressure or liquidity strain before then.

thesis: The 60-day price surge and volume spike are explained by a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: Veeva's fiscal Q2 2027 earnings report (August 26, 2026) beat consensus on revenue ($928M vs ~$905M est., +17.6-18% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS ($2.35 vs ~$2.22 est.), while management raised full-year FY2027 revenue and EPS guidance, with CEO Peter Gassner citing Vault CRM's 'best quarter ever' (180+ live customers including five top-20 biopharma accounts) as an AI-driven adoption catalyst; the move is company-specific and fundamentals-driven, not a technical or sector-wide pattern, even though the stock is now up ~40% in 60 days and sits only ~9% below its 52-week high, which raises near-term valuation and mean-reversion risk. A secondary supportive factor is the August 2025 settlement of the long-running IQVIA litigation, which removed a legal overhang ahead of this quarter's results.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if Veeva's next quarterly report (Q3 FY2027, historically reported in mid-to-late November) shows decelerating Vault CRM/subscription growth, a guidance cut, or margin compression, or if shares give back a substantial portion of the post-earnings gap (e.g., sustained close back below the pre-earnings ~$245 level), indicating the rally was a one-time re-rating rather than a durable trend.
